Why Does My Complexion Differ From Looking in the Mirror Rather in Pictures?
When a picture is taken, when it is retouched color is usually balanced. This can make a picture hotter or cooler depending on what the white is set as.

1. Mirrors show an inverted image, while pictures usually do not.
  2. Most people's bathroom have what photographers call soft light (even light from a large light source that casts few shadows--like a cloudy day). Most non-professionals' photographs are taken in hard light (mid-day sun or in most of the other rooms of most homes where the light is provided by one or a few point sources of light). As an example, hard light is on the left, soft light is on the right.
  3. Also, in your bathroom, you are limited by perception which means your brain can both feedback on your muscles to magnify good traits and minimize bad traits, and your brain does a huge amount of image processing from memory rather than direct eye input.
